text:
incident-bot: PAGER: INCIDENT PGB-92 — inference-frontend reporting spike in 5xx and tail latency. Severity: high. Incident page: https://incidents.redwood.ai/PGB-92. Paging oncall.

Alex H: I'm on it — seeing ~25% 5xx on hosted /v1/generate and elevated latencies in eu-west-1. Taking initial ownership, will triage root cause. ETA 5m for initial findings.

Maya R: i'll stay for the next 30m to hand off if needed. @Alex H do you want me to take comms or stay as secondary?

Alex H: Thanks. I can start triage but my shift ends in ~20m. Prefer to hand driving to someone who will be around for the next 2+ hours. Who's available to take over as driver?

Sam C: I can take comms (post updates to status page + customers slack). Not ideal to drive right now, but can be comms until someone else takes driver.

Jordan L: I can take driver for the overnight window — I have capacity. Jordan driving, Sam comms, Maya secondary for context, Alex do a quick handover summary.

Alex H: Ok assigning per above. Quick state: errors started at 02:12 UTC, error type: 5xx downstream from model-serving (grpc timeout -> 504). Rolling windows show queue depth spike on certain GPU nodes. Autoscaler didn't add capacity due to a config bug. No evidence of data loss. Customer impact: elevated latency and some failed requests for hosted customers. Mitigation in progress: draining suspect nodes and routing to healthy pool.

ops-scribe: Runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pgb-incident (see "assign-driver-and-comms" section). Checklist:
1) Confirm owner
2) Post on status page
3) Drain nodes and attach fallback
4) Start timeline in incident doc

Alex H: Commands I ran just now (paste for handoff):
```
# check pods & queues
kubectl get pods -n inference | grep gpu
curl -s https://metrics.redwood.ai/query?expr=queue_depth | jq .
# drain node X
kubectl cordon node/gpu-23
kubectl drain node/gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

Jordan L: Got it. I'm the new driver. I'll finish the drain for the remaining suspect nodes and validate routing. Sam, can you post the first customer update? Use this templated blurb: "We are investigating increased errors and latency for the hosted inference API. Engineers are actively mitigating. No ETA yet." I'll update once routing is stable.

Sam C: Will post now to status and slack. Tagging SIG: @support-team, @product-ops. :loudspeaker:

Maya R: I'll hang tight for another 25m and cover any context gaps. If Jordan needs me later, I can jump in as secondary.

Alex H: Thanks team. Remaining items for handoff: note recent config change that suppressed autoscaler alarms (PR #4021), link: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/infra/pulls/4021. Jordan, please check autoscaler policy and re-enable alerting after you confirm routing is healthy.

Jordan L: On it. Re-enabling alerts after verification. I'll update the incident doc and set next steps for the morning shift. If anything regresses, please page @oncall.

incident-bot: INCIDENT PGB-92 updated: driver=Jordan L, comms=Sam C, secondary=Maya R. Timeline: https://incidents.redwood.ai/PGB-92/timeline

Jordan L: Handoff complete from Alex — Alex, thanks for the quick triage. Alex, if you're available for a 5m post-handoff sync in DMs that would be helpful but no pressure.

Alex H: Available for 5. Leaving the channel. Good luck team. :thumbsup:

Sam C: Status page posted and customer messages queued. Will post any major changes here.
